units.function: Unit tests deciding whether a Google Sheets tool-gallery entry is available by extracting a service-account robot email from instance environment JSON or a filesystem path.
units.dependencyDirection: Ambient process environment or a configured host file is parsed by tool-access service code and reduced to an availability/reason/robotEmail projection.
units.lifecycle: Inline JSON wins or a JSON file is read; a client email makes the integration available, while absent configuration fails closed with an English reason.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover inline, file and missing configuration. Missing are malformed/oversized JSON, file permission/symlink/path attacks, precedence, secret redaction, credential validity/expiry, per-Company isolation, vault references, authorization, Sheets scope, data egress and stable error codes independent of English prose.
units.designRationale: Show a ready-to-use gallery capability when an operator preconfigures one instance-wide service account.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Company-scoped Data Connectors, explicit data authorization contracts and egress controls rather than ambient global credentials.
units.companyOsFit: Reject instance-environment ownership as the production model. Google Sheets becomes a DataConnector adapter using SecretPort handles, immutable credential versions, Company/data-set scopes, consented Robot identity, health attestation and export policy; the gallery consumes only a safe capability projection.
units.responsibilityConflict: An instance environment silently makes a credential available to the product without proving which Company/data owner authorized it, which Sheets are allowed or who is responsible for exports. Robot email discovery is not a data contract.

units.function: Unit tests filtering filesystem changes that should restart the development server.
units.dependencyDirection: Repository-relative paths enter a development script predicate; generated worktrees/reports/tests/config are ignored while runtime source remains restart-relevant.
units.keyDataModels: Repository path patterns for generated state, reports, test/spec directories/config and runtime source.
units.lifecycle: File watcher events are classified into ignored or restart-triggering paths.
units.testAssessment: Representative exclusions and inclusions are covered. Missing are Windows separators/case, rename/symlink paths, generated runtime assets, new test naming conventions and end-to-end watcher behavior.
units.designRationale: Reduce noisy development restarts caused by tests, diagnostics and Agent worktree activity.
units.companyOsProblem: This affects contributor ergonomics and upstream maintenance, not the product runtime.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the focused watcher predicate if Company OS adopts a similar monorepo dev runner; do not copy Paperclip-specific paths into production architecture.
units.responsibilityConflict: None directly; ignored changes can only weaken local verification if developers assume the server restarted.

units.function: Unit tests for bounded subprocess-output capture and maximum-size JSON HTTP response parsing in development orchestration.
units.dependencyDirection: Arbitrary string/Buffer chunks append to a bounded tail buffer, while Fetch Response bytes enter a size-limited JSON parser.
units.keyDataModels: Byte limit, captured tail text, totalBytes/truncated and parsed JSON response.
units.lifecycle: Small output is retained exactly; oversized output keeps only a marked tail and total count. JSON within limit parses, while oversized input rejects before parsing completes.
units.testAssessment: Core limit semantics and mixed string/Buffer append are covered. Missing are split multibyte UTF-8, zero/negative limits, huge single chunks, streaming cancellation/backpressure, misleading Content-Length, invalid JSON/content type and secret redaction.
units.designRationale: Prevent verbose child processes or health endpoints from exhausting orchestrator memory while retaining useful diagnostics.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector execution and evidence ingestion need hard byte/event limits without losing a verifiable reference to truncated content.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT bounded streaming primitives inside Connector nodes; add UTF-8-safe truncation, cancellation/backpressure, per-stream limits, redaction, full-content hash/object-store evidence reference and structured truncation metadata.
units.responsibilityConflict: A retained tail is diagnostic context, not complete evidence. Company OS must never present truncated output as the full Agent result without an explicit completeness flag and hash/reference.

units.function: Filesystem test resolving development-watch ignore paths for symlinked UI dependencies/build output and sibling Paperclip worktrees.
units.dependencyDirection: A server root inside a generated worktree is mapped to logical UI paths, real symlink targets, shared worktree roots and global dependency/cache globs.
units.keyDataModels: Server/worktree/shared UI roots, symlink and real paths, recursive glob patterns for node_modules/Vite/dist/worktrees.
units.lifecycle: Watcher setup enumerates both visible symlinks and canonical targets so dependency caches, build output and sibling worktrees cannot trigger restart storms.
units.testAssessment: A realistic temporary symlink tree covers logical/real paths and recursive globs. Missing are broken links, permissions, non-worktree roots, platform-specific junctions/case, path escape and an end-to-end proof that relevant source remains watched.
units.designRationale: Avoid feedback loops and resource spikes in a multi-worktree development environment with shared UI directories.
units.companyOsProblem: Useful only for contributor workflow if Company OS later uses shared worktrees/FDE development tooling.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the canonical-path plus logical-path ignore strategy; keep it isolated from product runtime and derive repository-specific paths dynamically.
units.responsibilityConflict: None in production; overly broad ignores can hide local source changes and weaken the developer's verification evidence.
